## Facts (4):
- [convention] Feature flags in the notifier (id: 01a10b2e-1f12-7420-bb3d-c1e4c97a7658; source: shared/human)
  The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.
- [convention] Feature flags go through flags.is_on() (id: 01a10b2d-3b01-78d2-bbb4-4352e0a36215; source: shared/human)
  Read feature flags only with `flags.is_on("name")` from src/flags.py. Flag names are kebab-case and must be declared in flags.toml.
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10b2d-9477-7ad3-a16e-4ac00ca85c5e; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10b2d-c410-7763-b26e-85317233c733; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.","hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

`send_receipt` in `services/notifier/notifier/email.py` is now gated behind the `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_EMAIL` environment variable. The notifier tests pass (2 passed).

- **Flag:** the flag is on only when `NOTIFIER_FF_RECEIPT_EMAIL` is `"1"`. This follows the notifier convention, because the deployed function can't read the root `flags.toml`.
- **Off behaviour:** when the flag is off, `send_receipt` returns `None` and sends nothing. Any caller that uses the returned message id needs to handle `None`.
- **Tests:** in `tests/test_email.py` I set the flag in the existing test and added one for the flag-off case.
- **Rollout:** this flag is all-or-nothing per deployment. Turning it on for a share of users would need a percentage or per-customer check, which the env-var convention doesn't provide. I can add one if you want it.
- **What I gated:** there was no separate new receipt email in the code, only the existing `send_receipt`. `render()` is also still a stub, and there is no `templates/` directory. If the new email is a different one, tell me which and I'll move the gate.

I didn't commit anything.
